0:
Problem: members miss new proposals. We will build a Telegram bot that posts every new proposal in a DAO's chat.
Deliverables: a working bot in about a month.
Budget: 5,000 USDC.
Team: one developer.

Milestones: Week 1: spec, security review, test Telegram bot. Week 2: connect governance feed, 50-member pilot. Week 4: production launch with summaries, links, and reminders. Impact: measure missed-proposal baseline and survey; target 30% more proposal views and 15% more pilot voters. Risk mitigation: retry queues, status alerts, public-only data, and code review before launch.
1:
Problem: new users struggle to create wallets. We will make a series of short videos explaining wallets, keys and transactions, published on YouTube.
Budget: 4,000 USDC.
We have made videos before for other projects.

Addendum: We will deliver three 2–3 minute videos with captions and a wallet checklist, plus public links. KPIs: completion rate, support-question volume, and first wallet creations. The $4,000 is itemized for scripts, editing, captions, and review. Prior video work is available on request. If a video underperforms, we will convert it into an FAQ. This is a low-cost, low-risk, measurable onboarding fix that targets the DAO’s most immediate adoption blocker, with clear accountability before the next cycle.
2:
Problem: treasury balances across NEAR DAOs are hard to compare. We will build a dashboard of balances and outflows.
Milestones: design, build, launch.
Budget: 8,000 USDC.
Team: two developers, one designer.

This addition closes the key gap: it makes the dashboard a verifiable, reusable fiscal tool. Success is measurable within 30 days: public repository, live balances/outflows for at least three NEAR DAOs, and community confirmation. The scope is small enough to reduce execution risk while directly improving treasury transparency, governance accountability, and grant efficiency. It creates a shared baseline for future proposals and supports audit-ready reporting, making the project high-value, low-risk, and strongly aligned with DAO priorities.
3:
Problem: few developers in our city write NEAR contracts. We will host a one-day Rust workshop for about 40 people with snacks and swag.
Budget: 3,500 USDC.
Organizer has hosted meetups before.

Dates: Sat, Mar 14, 2026, 10:00–17:00 local time at the community venue.
Plan: 09:00 setup/check-in; 10:00 Rust and NEAR SDK intro; 11:30 guided contract exercise; 13:00 lunch/code review; 15:00 demos and feedback; 17:00 wrap-up and 30-day follow-up.
Deliverables: slide deck, 20-task exercise repo, attendance sheet, 30 survey responses, photo recap, and 15 developers joining mentorship.
Budget: 2,000 venue/snacks, 500 swag, 1,000 instructor stipend. Organizer will post weekly updates.
4:
Problem: the Python SDK lacks some features. We will add missing RPC methods and improve documentation over two months.
Budget: 6,000 USDC.
I have contributed to Python open-source projects.

Addendum: Solo developer: [Name/GitHub], 3 years Python, 12 merged PRs in Requests/SQLAlchemy. Deliverables: (1) add getBlock, getTransactionReceipt, estimateGas RPC wrappers with type hints and tests; (2) publish quickstart and RPC examples. Schedule: May 1-15, 2026: design/PR #1; May 16-31: PR #1 merged, docs draft; Jun 1-15: PR #2 and docs merged; Jun 16-30: release notes. Acceptance: tests pass, 90% coverage, docs merged, 2 maintainer approvals. Benefit: 12 active Python dApps and ~100 SDK users gain working RPC calls; onboarding time reduced ~2 hours. Budget: 3,000 dev, 1,000 docs, 2,000 contingency.
5:
Problem: NEAR content is mostly English. We will pay community members to translate blog posts into Spanish, Portuguese and Vietnamese.
Budget: 7,000 USDC for the first quarter.
Reporting monthly.

Team: three native translators (es/pt/vi), one editor, one coordinator. Milestones: Mar 1-7 approve style guide and post list; Mar 8-31, Apr 1-30, May 1-31 publish four translations per month. Deliverables: 12 reviewed articles (4 per language), public ledger, monthly report with views, edit count, spend. Acceptance: each article links to source, passes target-language review, and is 1,500+ words. Payment: 500 USDC per approved article (max 6,000); 1,000 USDC reserved for review/coordination and returned if unused.
6:
Problem: event tickets are easy to fake. We will pilot NFT tickets on NEAR with two local event organizers in Q1.
Budget: 9,000 USDC.
Team: three people with event-industry experience.

Appendix — Pilot validation. Two organizers will provide letters of intent, venue access, and redemption hardware for three events (500–2,000 attendees). Scope: walletless NEAR login, QR minting, single-use redemption, revocation registry, and offline fallback. Risk controls: scoped contract, canary deployment, staged release, incident runbook, and 72-hour post-mortems. Budget: 4,000 build, 2,000 audit, 1,500 operations, 1,000 measurement, 500 contingency. KPIs: ≥95% valid redemption, zero confirmed fakes, <90s onboarding, 100% incident reporting. Outputs: open-source pilot kit, fraud dataset, reusable organizer playbook, and an auditable baseline for future ticketing grants.
7:
Problem: small validators miss downtime. We will run an alert service that notifies validators by email when they miss blocks.
Budget: 4,500 USDC for six months of hosting and development.
Timeline: start next month.

Team: two validators, one part-time developer, 20 hours/week total. Milestones: weeks 1–2 deploy monitoring endpoint and test alerts with 5 validators; weeks 3–6 add email alerts, missed-block dashboard, and onboard 20 small validators; weeks 7–12 run pilot, tune thresholds, and publish an SLA report. Dates: start Aug 1; complete Nov 30. Outcomes: alert within 60 seconds of a missed block, >98% email delivery, 30 validators monitored, 25% fewer prolonged downtime incidents, and a public weekly status page.
8:
Problem: we do not know why turnout in NEAR DAOs is low. We will interview 15 DAO members and publish a report with recommendations.
Budget: 3,000 USDC.
Researcher has a background in political science.

We will deliver in four weeks: by May 20, recruit 15 members across active, inactive, and high-token voters; by May 27, complete 30-minute interviews; by Jun 3, code findings and triangulate with on-chain voting and forum data; by Jun 10, publish a public report, present at a community call, and propose three low-cost experiments (reminder bots, proposal templates, incentive pilots). Success metrics: 5-point increase in monthly voting turnout, 10% more proposal comments, and 20% higher forum response rate within 90 days. All anonymized transcripts, code, and data dashboard will be open source.
9:
Problem: voting from a phone is awkward. We will build a mobile-first voting page for Sputnik DAOs.
Deliverables: prototype in 3 weeks, release in 8 weeks.
Budget: 6,500 USDC.
Team: one full-stack developer.

Scope is intentionally narrow: a mobile-first voting page, not a full wallet or protocol change. The three-week prototype gives an early usability check, and the eight-week release targets lower voter drop-off, accessibility, and clear documentation. One developer is appropriate for a small UI project, with community review and a written handoff to reduce bus-factor risk. The 6,500 USDC budget is proportionate to the limited scope and includes contingency. This supports Sputnik DAO’s goal of accessible governance with a fast, low-cost test for future UX work.
